paragraphs.text: Junius observeth that this and the two following prophecies, viz., those in Eze 7:1-27; Eze 8:1-18, were delivered on the Sabbath day; that is the proper season for preaching.
paragraphs.anchor: And the word of the Lord came unto me.

paragraphs.text: i.e., The Jews, who are haughty, and hard as mountains, who are asperi et inculti, rough and rude, as mountaineers use to be. In Mount Olivet itself, besides other mountains, they boldly set up their idols, even in the sight of the Lord; so that he never looked out of the sanctuary but he beheld that vile hill of abominations; called therefore, by an elegant alliteration, the Hill of Corruption. {2Ki 23:13}
paragraphs.anchor: Set thy face toward the mountains of Israel

paragraphs.text: Because ye are polluted by man’s sins, and so made hateful unto me. For as God thinks the better of the places wherein he is sincerely served, yea, where his saints are born, {Psa 87:5} or make abode, {Isa 49:16} so the worse of such places where Satan’s seat is.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, I, even I, will bring a sword upon you.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Your sun images, whence also Jupiter Hammon had his name, which Macrobius {a} saith was the same with the sun. See 2Ch 23:5.
paragraphs.anchor: Your images shall be broken down.

paragraphs.text: Cruentatos vulneratos, vel interfectos vestros; such as when wounded, fly to their idols for safety.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will cast down your slain men.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Your dii stercorei, dunghill deities, more loathsome than any excrements.
paragraphs.anchor: Before your idols.

paragraphs.text: {a} Lib. i. Sat., cap. 23.
That in the very places where they have sinned there they may suffer. So in the valley of Hinnom, and at Pilate’s praetorium, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will lay the dead carcases of the children of Israel, &c.

paragraphs.text: Omnia everram et evertam funditus. I will turn all topsy-turvy.
paragraphs.anchor: In all your dwelling places.

paragraphs.text: Those toilsome toys, your idols and monuments of idolatry. This the prophet telleth them again and again, that he might waken them, and work them to repentance.
paragraphs.anchor: Your works shall be abolished.

paragraphs.text: That I am dicti mei Dominus, one that will be as good as my word. So shall all, not idolaters only, but broachers of heresies also, quae furore et foetere cultores suos faciunt, saith Oecolampadius here.
paragraphs.anchor: And ye shall know that I am the Lord.

paragraphs.text: For royal use. See on Eze 5:3.
paragraphs.anchor: Yet will I leave a remnant.

paragraphs.text: Here beginneth that true repentance never to be repented of. {Psa 22:27; Psa 20:7}
paragraphs.anchor: And they that escape of you shall remember me.

paragraphs.text: i.e., I am troubled, saith Piscator. I am tired out, saith Zegedine, and made to break off the course of my kindness. I am broken off from their whorish heart - so Polanus rendereth it; that is, saith he, I leave them, though loath to do it: the breach is merely on their part; for they have an impetus, a spirit of whoredoms in them, that causeth them to err, and go whoring from under their God. {Hos 4:12; Hos 9:1}
paragraphs.anchor: Because I am broken off from their whorish heart

paragraphs.text: Those windows of wickedness through which the devil (who is ειδωλοχαρης, as saith Synesius) doth oft wind himself into the soul.
paragraphs.anchor: And with their eyes.

paragraphs.text: {a} They shall displease themselves, saith the Vulgate; but that is not enough. Pudefient in faciebus suis, say others. They shall bleed inwardly, and blush outwardly, deeply detesting their former abominations, and not waiting till others condemn them, they shall condemn themselves.
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall loathe themselves.

paragraphs.text: {a} κοψονται. - Sept.
By woeful experience. He that trembleth not in sinning shall be crushed to pieces in feeling, said blessed Bradford.
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall know.

paragraphs.text: In terrorem only,
paragraphs.anchor: And that I have not said in vain.

paragraphs.text: Sic ait Dominator Dominus.
paragraphs.anchor: Thus saith the Lord God.

paragraphs.text: Manibus pedibusque obnixe omnia facito; do thine utmost by gestures and speeches to make this stupid people perceive their sin and danger.
paragraphs.anchor: Smite with thine hand.

paragraphs.text: Propter omnes abominationes pessimas; { a} we cannot call sin bad enough; the worst word in a man’s belly is too good for it. O perdita Israel, dicere vult, quae tot malas abominationes operata es, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: Alas for all the evil abominations.

paragraphs.text: {a} Oecolamp.
Pluribus verbis hunc locum tractat. Ointments must not only be laid upon the part that acheth, but also robbed and chafed in; so must menaces and promises, that they may soak and sink into the soul.
paragraphs.anchor: He that is far off shall die of the pestilence.

paragraphs.text: Vexatio dabit intellectum; smart shall make wit. See Eze 6:10. Four times in this chapter are these words used: Verba toties inculcata, viva sunt, vera sunt, sana sunt, plana sunt. {a} The words are driven home often, they are alive, they are true, they are wholesome, they are plain.
paragraphs.anchor: Then shall ye know that I am the Lord.

paragraphs.text: See on Eze 6:4.
paragraphs.anchor: Among their idols.

paragraphs.text: Idolatry is costly.
paragraphs.anchor: Where they did offer sweet savour.

paragraphs.text: {a} Augustine.
Which was horriditate nobile, bordering upon that terrible howling wilderness mentioned by Moses. {Deu 8:15 Jer 48:22}
paragraphs.anchor: Than the wilderness toward Diblath.
